not_modelled.what: Additional standard deduction of 850 (single, head of household) or 700 (joint, separate) per box for a blind filer or spouse.
Exemptions of 2,320 for each dependent, each child born in the year and a stillbirth.
Additional exemption of 2,320 for each honorably discharged veteran certified by the VA at the 100% disability rate; a projection does not know this.
Thrift Savings Plan distributions are subtracted on line A14; a projection cannot tell them from other employer-plan distributions, which are taxed.
IRA or plan withdrawals of money first received as a KPERS lump sum at retirement and rolled over, with earnings, are subtracted on line A11; a projection cannot trace rolled-over money.
Retirement annuity contracts for State Board of Regents faculty and staff are subtracted on line A14 (not after a rollover into an unrelated plan); a projection cannot tell them from other annuities.
A one-time KPERS lump sum of withdrawn accumulated contributions is subtracted on line A25.
Interest and dividends from U.S. government obligations are subtracted on line A12.

approximations.what: The Kansas standard deduction is always taken; Kansas itemized deductions (Schedule A) are not modelled.
approximations.size: 5.58% of the amount by which Kansas itemized deductions exceed the standard deduction, for an itemizer.

approximations.what: A qualifying surviving spouse files as Head of Household in Kansas (PDF page 6), but the schema gives this status the joint brackets; the deductions are correct.
Every public_pension is treated as exempt, but line A14 names particular Kansas plans and only 'certain' first class city pensions; a Kansas local plan not on the list is taxable.
approximations.size: 5.58% of such a pension; for a 30,000 pension, 1,674 a year.

approximations.what: A pension from another state's government, private pensions, IRA and other employer-plan distributions and Roth conversions stay in Kansas income: no line subtracts them. This is read from the booklet's silence, not from a sentence saying they are taxed.
approximations.size: None if the reading is right; otherwise 5.58% of the income.

approximations.what: Thrift Savings Plan distributions, KPERS rollover withdrawals and Regents annuities are taxed (not_modelled).
approximations.size: 5.58% of the qualifying amount; for a 30,000 withdrawal, 1,674 a year.

approximations.what: The blind amount, dependent exemptions and disabled veteran exemption are not applied (not_modelled).
approximations.size: Up to 5.58% of 850 = 47.43 per blind box or 5.58% of 2,320 = 129.46 per exemption, a year.

approximations.what: Interest on U.S. government obligations is taxed (the projection cannot tell it from other interest).
A projection that cannot tell Kansas bonds from other states' bonds treats all tax-exempt interest as other-state and adds it back.
approximations.size: 5.58% of the interest from exempt Kansas obligations.

approximations.what: Line 11 Kansas tax on a lump sum distribution (13% of the federal tax on Form 4972) is not computed.
approximations.size: 13% of the federal Form 4972 tax, in a year with such a distribution.

approximations.what: Line A2 add-back of current KPERS and similar members' salary contributions is not computed (the projection does not know them).
Earned income credit, child and dependent care credit, credit for taxes paid to other states and the property tax refunds are not applied (outside the record).
approximations.size: Depends on the household; none for most retired households without other-state tax.

approximations.what: Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
approximations.size: Under 2 a year: a table row spans 50 of income (1.40 at 5.58%) and is within 0.50 of the schedule at its midpoint; the worksheet differs by 0.40 (single group) or 0.20 (joint).
